title: Conditional graphs versus unobserved quantum mixtures
description: Secondary descriptive controls: reset matter to a fresh product and freeze each graph. Mean graph-conditioned F, F of averaged conditional responses, and F of the unobserved mixture are different quantities. High conditional capture can coexist with tiny valid or connected graph mass.
uncertainty: No confidence intervals or new hypothesis test. Copied means, SDs and ranges describe independent E preparations; deterministic Splus/Sempty use one specified state and null SD. Defined and undefined unit counts and all graph-validity masses are retained.
sampleUnit: 216 archived aggregate rows over 168 preparations: E uses 12 independent units per cell; Splus/Sempty one. Born, density and degree laws are exact weighted graph controls on the same finite catalogues, not extra independent physical evidence.
assumptions: An accessible graph record and a frozen Hamiltonian change the operational protocol. Undefined graph-conditioned F mass is reported rather than discarded. No connectivity postselection is used. These controls do not change the registered unconditioned NO-GO.
selection: All 216 existing aggregates, all ten metric objects flattened into scalar suffix columns, and the separate pooled conditional ratio. No per-preparation means are newly pooled, no intervals are invented, and the 1,008 detailed secondary unit rows remain in the linked source.
